'''''Platyhypnidium alopecuroides''''', or '''Portuguese feather-moss''', is a species of moss from the family [[Brachytheciaceae]], first described in 2000.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Platyhypnidium alopecuroides (Brid.) Koperski & Sauer, M. — The Plant List |url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/tro-35216703 |access-date=30 October 2020 |website=www.theplantlist.org}}</ref> It is an [[Aquatic plant|aquatic moss]] and is normally found growing in rocky streams.<ref name="rbge">{{Cite web |last=Blockeel |first=Tom |title=Platyhypnidium alopecuroides |url=https://websites.rbge.org.uk/bbs/activities/mosses/Platyhypnidium%20alopecuroides.pdf |access-date=30 October 2020 |website=Royal Botanic Garden of Edinburgh}}</ref>

==Description==
''Platyhypnidium alopecuroides'' is a green to brownish aquatic moss. The stems grow to approximately 10 cm in length and have few branches. The [[cataphyll|leaves]] are 2-3mm in length, concave and grow overlapping each other, giving it a cylindrical look.<ref name="rbge"/>

==Habitat==
It grows on rocks in fast flowing streams and can be found in both open and wooded areas.<ref name="rbge"/>
